title: “And, Carpenter, how do these unwholesome thoughts arise? Their arising has also been taught. It should be said that they arise from perception. What is…
content: “And, Carpenter, how do these unwholesome thoughts arise? Their arising has also been taught. It should be said that they arise from perception. What is perception? There are various perceptions, many and diverse: sensual perception, ill-will perception, harmfulness perception. From these, unwholesome thoughts arise.”

title: “Monks, I do not see any other class of things that is as diverse as the mind. Those beings in the animal realm — such…
content: “Monks, I do not see any other class of things that is as diverse as the mind. Those beings in the animal realm — such beings are diverse because of their minds. Therefore, monks, one should constantly reflect on one’s own mind thus: ‘For a long time, this mind has been defiled by greed, hatred, and delusion. Through the defilement of the mind, beings are defiled. Through the purification of the mind, beings are purified.’”

title: “Monks, there are these three kinds of craving. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. These, monks, are the three…
content:
“Monks, there are these three kinds of craving. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. These, monks, are the three kinds of craving.

Bound by the bondage of craving,
Their minds attached to becoming and non-becoming,
Bound by Māra’s bondage,
Those beings are not secure from bondage.
They go on in the wandering,
Gone to birth and death.

But those who have abandoned craving,
Free from craving for becoming and non-becoming,
Having reached the far shore,
In this very world, they have attained
The destruction of the defilements.”

title: “One who clings, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.” - “I understand, Blessed One! I…
content: “One who clings, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.” - “I understand, Blessed One! I understand, Well-gone One!” - “How, monk, do you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement?” - “One who clings to form, venerable sir, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling … to perception … to formations … to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. Venerable sir, I understand in detail the meaning of the Blessed One’s brief statement thus.” - “Good, good, monk! Good, monk! Thus you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement. One who clings to form, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling … to perception … to formations … to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.”

title: “Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful…
content: “Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is a samana.”

title: Elder Uttarapāla: I am truly virtuous, Reflecting on good purpose. I have abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure, Which are the world’s confusion. Born…
content:
Elder Uttarapāla:

I am truly virtuous,
Reflecting on good purpose.
I have abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,
Which are the world’s confusion.

Born in Māra’s realm,
Struck by strong darts,
Yet I have escaped
Māra’s snare.

All sensual desires are destroyed,
All forms of existence are demolished.
The path of birth and death is ended —
Now there is no further becoming.

title: The Blessed One replied to Bhadrāvudha: “Having expelled all desire for household things, Above, below, across, and in between — Whatever one clings to in…
content:
The Blessed One replied to Bhadrāvudha:
“Having expelled all desire for household things,
Above, below, across, and in between —
Whatever one clings to in the world,
By that very thing, Māra follows one.

Therefore, the wise one, knowing this,
Does not cling to anything in the world.
The mindful monk, seeing that beings
Are attached to what they cling to,
In Māra’s realm,
Should not long for any possession.”

title: “Deep, Ānanda, is this dependent origination, and deep indeed is its definition. It is because of not understanding, not penetrating this Dhamma, Ānanda, that beings…
content: “Deep, Ānanda, is this dependent origination, and deep indeed is its definition. It is because of not understanding, not penetrating this Dhamma, Ānanda, that beings are tangled like a ball of thread, covered with blight, like muñja grass, like bulrushes, unable to escape from the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower realm, saṃsāra. Ānanda, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are clung to — craving increases. With craving as condition, existence comes to be. With existence as condition, birth comes to be. With birth as condition, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Such is the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Just as, Ānanda, a great tree, having its roots that extend downward and laterally, all those roots convey the sap upwards — that great tree, being nourished and sustained in such a way, would stand for a long time. So too, Ānanda, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are clung to — craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging comes to be … Such is the origination of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: “Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should…
content: “Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling … perception … formations … consciousness there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all consciousness should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Rādha, knowing thus, seeing thus, regarding this conscious body and all external signs, there is no ‘I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit.’”

title: “And what, Ānanda, is the perception of peril? Here, Ānanda, a monk, going to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an…
content: “And what, Ānanda, is the perception of peril? Here, Ānanda, a monk, going to the forest, to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, reflects: ‘This body is of much suffering, of much peril. Various diseases arise in this body, such as: eye disease, ear disease, nose disease, tongue disease, body disease, head disease, ear-edge disease, mouth disease, tooth disease, cough, asthma, catarrh, fever, aging, abdominal pain, fainting, dysentery, colic, cholera, leprosy, boils, eczema, tuberculosis, epilepsy, skin disease, itch, scab, ringworm, scabies, blood-bile disorder, diabetes, hemorrhoids, cancer, sores, ulcerations; diseases born of bile, born of phlegm, born of wind, born of the combination of humors; diseases born of change of season, born of improper behavior, born of sudden assault, born of the result of kamma; cold, heat, hunger, thirst, defecation, urination.’ Thus he dwells contemplating peril in this body.”
